plant-based diets, which emphasize legumes, vegetables, fruits and whole grains, and discourage most or almost all animal foods, can be an effective tool for preventing and treating diabetes.

a plant-based diet is effective in preventing and treating type diabetes and that a plant-based approach to diabetes prevention and treatment is a promising strategy for improving the health of individuals at high risk for developing type 2 diabetes.

In summary, our research is concerned with
plant-based diet for diabetes.
the role of a plant-based dietary pattern in the prevention and treatment for type 2 Diabetes.
the role of plant foods, including whole grains, vegetables and fruits, nuts, seeds, and legumes, and their components (e.g., fiber, phytonutrients) in the prevention and treatment type 2 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

plant-based diets, especially those rich in whole plant foods and low in refined grains and added sugars and solid fats, can play a role in preventing type 2 diabetes, improving diabetes control, and preventing diabetes-related complications.
plant-based diets are beneficial for the prevention and management type 2 diabetes.
plant-based diets are effective in preventing and treating type diabetes and that the benefits are largely due to the types and sources of macronutrients and micronutrients in these diets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a plant-based diet is associated with lower rates of diabetes and cardiovascular disease, and may be associated with lower rates and mortality from some cancers.
a diet rich in plant foods and low in animal products is associated with lower risk of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
a plant-based diet, which is rich in vegetables, fruits, whole grains, and legumes, is an effective and healthy dietary pattern for the prevention and management type 2 diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a plant-based diet is a viable, evidence-based approach for preventing and treating diabetes.
a plant-based diet, especially one rich in whole grains, legumes, vegetables, fruits and nuts, is a healthy eating pattern that is effective for the prevention and management type 2 diabetes.

the plant-based dietary patterns that are most beneficial in preventing and treating type 2 diabetes are those that emphasize unrefined plant foods (vegetables, fruit, legumes, whole grain, and nuts), minimize processed foods, and include a variety of plant foods to provide a broad range of phytonutrients and fiber.
